theme: Ship a new game prototype as a team of three in a 2-day hackathon
summary: Built "Kodama", a 2D action game where you see a pitch-black cave through ripples of sound. I owned everything that shapes how the game feels — ripples, sound, light, vibration — plus the team's development infrastructure.

learnings.title: Turning scenes into text killed our merge conflicts
learnings.body: Unity scene files become unresolvable conflicts once three people touch them. I built a round-trip tool that generates a whole scene from a custom text DSL and exports existing scenes back out, replacing the binary blob with a diffable text asset

learnings.title: Cohesive feedback comes from event design
learnings.body: Simply putting the fall height on the landing event let the light, sound and vibration owners derive intensity from the same number with zero coordination, so all three reactions synced naturally

learnings.title: Prototype quality tracks how often you touch the real device
learnings.body: I automated APK build, install and launch behind a single shortcut so every teammate could try a tweak on a real phone the moment they thought of it

summary: Experienced a studio's full development flow in 5 days. Compiled C++ code to WebAssembly with Emscripten so the same game runs in the browser.

learnings.title: The main branch is protected
learnings.body: Worked under a rule requiring at least one review approval before merging

learnings.title: Merging deploys automatically
learnings.body: GitHub Actions detects merges into main and runs all the way to deployment

learnings.title: Saw why CI matters in production
learnings.body: Realized the CI practices from my personal projects are used in real studio workflows too
